column1: # Client optimizations applied by patching. They go only into the
# SteinBridge variants; the vanilla variant remains the baseline.
# LongHashMap.getHashedKey: the x^z hash collides massively on the chunks around the player.
# World.setActivePlayerChunksAndCheckLight: O(players x radius^2) per tick; runs with one representative per chunk.
# ThreadDownloadImageData.loadTexture: reads the skin from the cache on the render thread; the body now sends that to background threads.
# ContainerPlayer.<init>: recipe lookup on a freshly created (empty) 2x2 grid for each player; constructor only.
# The queue of geometry builders grows, and the second worker in the list triggers the missing ones.
# WorldChunkManager.getBiomeGenerator(pos, default): BiomeCache has no lock, and with N threads building chunks two
# would write together ("Getting biome" crash). One at a time (BiomeLock).
# Chunk packets (NetHandlerPlayClient: S21 = bcy.a(go), S26 = bcy.a(gp)): the sections
# are prepared on the network thread, on the first pass through the handler (ChunkPrepare), and
# fillChunk on the game thread only swaps them in.
# Terrain by region (ChunkArena): geometry in mapped buffers per region and one
# glMultiDrawArrays per run of chunks of the same region. With this, the VBO path
# drawing in renderBlockLayer (bfr.a(adf)), range returned in deleteGlResources (bht.a).
# Chunks adjacent to the player marked dirty only because the data arrived (ChunkSync): on the threads,
# not on the render thread. The marking in the chunk handlers opens the "arrival" mode; the
# ViewFrustum's setNeedsUpdate (bga.a) records the origin; the updateChunkNow of setupTerrain decides.
# GlStateManager: the MODELVIEW and TEXTURE stacks are kept in Java (GLMatrix); Stein GFX reads the finished
# matrices from there, and the fixed-function fallback sends only the finished MODELVIEW to the driver. Every matrix operation of the game goes through
# one of these methods — each with a single GL11 call site.
# Before each use of MODELVIEW by the driver, the pending matrix goes in a glLoadMatrixf.
# Names from the original jar (LWJGL 2); the renaming to LWJGL 3 still applies.
# Display list compilation: nothing is deferred in there.
# FontRenderer (avn): the immediate mode of each character (renderDefaultChar = a,
# renderUnicodeChar = b) goes to a batch, drawn with one glDrawArrays per text.
# A texture change (unicode page) closes the batch; same texture, it continues.
# Color (formatting code) and underline/strikethrough (Tessellator without texture) close the batch.
# The game's font replaced by another (TextHook): the drawing of each character inside renderStringAtPos, and the
# width of each character wherever the game measures text. With no font registered, the game's path applies.
# The chat on the grid is drawn in the HUD font: the splitting of each message into lines (GuiUtilRenderComponents.splitText,
# called by GuiNewChat.setChatLine) measures with the same font.
# RenderItem.renderModel(model, color, stack): the vertices depend only on model and
# color (apart from the item's tint); each pair becomes a display list recorded once.
# Check (checkItemModel): bytes that would go to the driver, before Tessellator.draw.
# A resource reload recreates the models: the old lists are deleted.
# DataWatcher.getWatchedObject (pz.j): the read without the ReadWriteLock (the map only
# changes structure when the entity is constructed).
# ItemStack.isItemEnchanted (zx.w): result stored in the ItemStack itself, in
# fields created here, and invalidated by a counter that goes up when "ench" changes
# in any NBT (NBTTagCompound's map replaced in the constructor).
# LayerArmorBase: the glint of each piece (renderGlint, in renderLayer) is recorded
# and the two passes come out grouped after the whole layer.
# FontRenderer: String.indexOf(char) on the fixed glyph and format-code
# strings becomes a table lookup (FontIndex), with the same result.
# Signs: splitText and getFormattedText of each line, redone every frame in
# TileEntitySignRenderer (bhj.a), are kept in fields of the text component
# (ChatComponentStyle, es). The generation goes up on each resource reload.
# Fancy clouds kept between frames (CloudCache): the game's renderCloudsFancy (bfr.c) only
# runs when the geometry changes, with Tessellator.draw detoured to copy the vertices; on the
# other frames the copy comes from a VBO, with the cloud offset in a translation.
# EffectRenderer.updateEffectAlphaLayer (bec.a(List)): dead particles are removed in a
# single pass (Particles), instead of the quadratic removeAll.
# (ChunkGraph): each chunk's neighbor in arithmetic on the ViewFrustum grid, and the
# visible faces of the camera's section kept while the camera and the blocks do not change.
# The search loop (ChunkGraph.bfsLoop at queue.isEmpty()) without allocating per visited chunk; the
# setupTerrain call in renderWorldPass keeps the arguments the search uses.
# Version of the compilations, for the search check (ChunkGraph.compiled): after each
# Entity and particle light kept between frames (LightCache): the body of
# Entity.getBrightnessForRender, fields on the entity and the light version (before each
# NibbleArray.set, the only light write path).
# The float brightness (Entity.getBrightness) that RendererLivingEntity.setBrightness asks for on each layer of each
# living entity per frame, kept the same way (LightCache.entityBrightness; only with the Stein renderer on, outside it the
# game's call): fields on the entity, with the sky darkening alongside the version.
# Block version (ChunkGraph.bump): before each block write in a section
# (ExtendedBlockStorage.set), each chunk data swap (Chunk.fillChunk) and each
# renderEntities (bfr.a(Lpk;Lbia;F)V): the chunk of each section kept by BlockPos, world and
# chunk map version (ChunkGraph.chunkAt), instead of a map lookup every frame.
# renderInfos loops over filtered copies (ChunkGraph): in renderBlockLayer, the layer loop (size/get)
# only on chunks with some used layer — the translucent reordering uses an
# iterator and stays on the whole list; in renderEntities, the two loops (iterator) only on chunks
# with an entity in the section or a tile entity. Entity version before each add/remove on the chunk.
# Status bar icons in a single draw (HudBatch): during renderPlayerStats (avo.d,
# called in renderGameOverlay), drawTexturedModalRect (avp.b) does not close the draw of
# each icon; Tessellator.draw goes out once, at the end.
# Ping and connection without waiting for reverse DNS (engine/NetAddress): Mojang's Netty checks the server name against the
# block list (getHostName) and, with a server given by IP, did a reverse DNS lookup — 4.5 s per ping and per entry. The getByName of the ping
# (OldServerPinger.ping) and of the connection (GuiConnecting) returns the address already carrying the typed name.
# Shared default skin (engine/AsyncSkins): the sbSharedSkin field keeps, in each ThreadDownloadImageData, the common default
# texture while the real skin has not arrived, and TextureManager's bind goes through here to choose between the
# two. Without this, the arrival of a crowd uploaded the same image once per player.
# Names redone every frame with the same result (engine/NameCache): the getDisplayName hover
# (NBT with a text UUID, for the hover event that the nametag does not even read), the lowercase of the whole text
# at each color code in renderStringAtPos and the "Dinnerbone" regular expression in rotateCorpse.
# ... the hover kept on the entity itself (a patcher field), instead of the WeakHashMap.
# New renderer, deferred entities (dev.xavier.stein.gfx.SteinEntityDeferred; only active with
# framebuffer switch in the middle of it, names after the bodies.
# Particles in the new renderer (step 4): the same recording around the two EffectRenderer passes.
# ... and the base drawing of each particle (EntityFX.renderParticle) written straight into the buffer (SteinParticles).
# ... the sky (renderSky) and the clouds (renderClouds) recorded in strict order, and the three fixed sky VBOs registered
# in the recording's fixed geometry when the game fills them (SteinSky): generateSky2 (o), generateSky (p), generateStars (q).
# ... rain and snow (renderRainSnow), world border, outline of the targeted block and cracking.
# ... and first person (renderHand: arm, held item, map, overlays), step 5.
# Lens post-processing (SteinPostFx): after renderWorld (bfk.b(FJ)V) in updateCameraAndRender, with the world and the
# hand done, before the game's shader group (spectator, F4) and the HUD.
# The video settings' showcase (showcase.Showcase): renderWorld draws its own world while it is open (the swap
# happens inside, the post-processing after still applies), and the real player's hand is not drawn in it.
# The depth clear before the hand (GlStateManager.clear(GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT) in renderWorldPass) takes the world's depth
# away: the edge smoothing copies it first.
# The state that the new renderer reads: lightmap coordinates (setLightmapTextureCoords, which
# GlStateManager does not store) and textures rewritten or deleted (SteinTextureArrays).
# Blocks with a tile entity (signs, chests...) stay on today's path: the sign writes its text without
# depth after the wood, and the deferred wood would cover it.
# New renderer: the damage color kept when the game turns it on (setBrightness/unsetBrightness;
# doRender's setDoRenderBrightness already goes through GameHooks.ghostHurt).
# New renderer, step 1: GlStateManager state changes deferred during the recorded pass
# (SteinLazyGl; only with -Dsteinbridge.gfx.lazyState=true). Solo mode: without the flush before, which the destination does.
# New renderer, steps 3 and 4: dynamic geometry recorded in the deferred pass (dev.xavier.stein.gfx.SteinTessCapture;
# only active with -Dsteinbridge.gfx.deferredEntities=true). Every Tessellator.draw of the game (except the call sites with their
# own detour: clouds in bfr.c, status bar in avp.b) goes through the capture: in the entity pass it becomes data in the groups
# by state; outside it, and while recording a display list, it is the original draw.
# Game texture filter (AbstractTexture.setBlurMipmapDirect and TextureUtil.setTextureBlurMipmap): RenderItem
# removes the atlas mipmap for each item and puts it back afterwards; the recorded item comes out with the filter from when it was recorded.
# Solo mode: the batch flush before the call is taken out of here; in the recorded pass the filter is only registered (it goes to the driver
# with the rest of the deferred state), without first sending all the deferred state to the driver on each item.
# Blocks with a tile entity recorded too (only with -Dsteinbridge.gfx.deferredTiles=true; the pause above becomes nothing): the
# cracking of the block being broken draws immediately, after what is already recorded.
# New renderer, step 2: the players' pose computed by us, on several threads (gfx/SteinPlayerPose; only active with
# calls RendererLivingEntity's doRender (the super) through here: an eligible player becomes data, the rest follows the game's own.
# The stored poses go out before each profiler section change in renderEntities (the last is "blockentities",
# before the tile entities); the list is cleared before each pass.
# New renderer, step 2, layers through our own pose (gfx/SteinPlayerPose): only for the check
# (-Dsteinbridge.gfx.poseCheck=true; outside it each hook is a boolean test). They note the stack matrix right
# after LayerHeldItem's postRenderArm and each postRender of LayerArrow and LayerCustomHead, to compare with
# New renderer, deferred edge cases (gfx/SteinGlTrack, SteinEntityDeferred, ArmorGlint; only act with the
# deferred renderer on, otherwise they are the original call).
# Blend alpha factors: GlStateManager.blendFunc(II) does not update the alpha in the cache, but the driver's glBlendFunc
# applies to both. The same call sites as SteinLazyGl above (these rules replace them, still in solo mode),
# keeping track of which was the last one emitted.
# The current normal (glNormal3f): the sign text and the arrow draw with light and no per-vertex normal.
# ... and at the call sites inside the entity pass (sign, arrow, name above the head, RendererLivingEntity's name,
# item frame name), through SteinLazyGl in solo mode: the normal does not depend on the rest of the state, so in the recorded pass
# only the pending batch of the moment goes out before, without sending all the deferred state to the driver on each sign and each name (outside it,
# Lights redone in the middle of the pass (RenderHelper.enableStandardItemLighting ends in glLightModel; the item frame's glPopAttrib
# restores the earlier ones): the pending draw goes out with the lights from when it was recorded.
# Enchanted leather: the glint re-emits only the first draw of each piece (the base), not the leather overlay.
# New renderer: the round shadow's draw (Render.renderShadow) marked — black texture, light irrelevant, recordable.
# DataWatcher: the watched objects of each entity in an array by id (DataWatchers), instead of the HashMap on each read.
# Entity.getFlag (pk.g; isSneaking, isInvisible, isBurning...): the flags byte (id 0) mirrored in an int on the entity
# (EntityFlags), without the three dependent loads entity -> DataWatcher -> array -> WatchableObject on each read. The
# DataWatcher's numeric getters (byte, short, int, float: health, skin parts...) read a long by id in the DataWatcher itself
# (DataWatchers, pz.sbM0..31): one cache miss instead of three or four. The mirrors follow
# WatchableObject.setObject (pz$a.a), the only one that writes the value after the constructor; the object's owner (the
# DataWatcher) is marked when it enters the array by id.
# New renderer: cached text (dev.xavier.stein.gfx.SteinTextCache; only in the deferred pass, with Stein GFX).
# The renderStringAtPos called by renderString builds each text once and then repeats the stored batches; the width
# requested by the name (renderLivingLabel) and by the sign (TileEntitySignRenderer) comes from a cache alongside. A resource
# New renderer, recorded texture coordinate generation (gfx/SteinTexGen): the glTexGen plane, which GlStateManager
# does not store (the eye one through the inverse of the modelview from when it was given). The End portal uses it.
# New renderer, step 7: the game's fixed-function pipeline goes through gfx/SteinCoreGl (in the usual context it goes to the driver
# as before; with Stein GFX, in a core context, it does not reach the driver or is tracked in Java).
# Viewport change and screen copy in the middle of a recorded pass (the menu panorama draws at 256x256, copies and
# blurs): what was recorded goes out first, at the viewport and screen of the moment. Through SteinGlTrack, which notes the viewport for the Stein pass
# Framebuffer and program bound by the game (OpenGlHelper: GL 3.0, ARB and EXT paths) and by mods: the same call, and the
# value noted (gl.SteinGlBindings) so the Stein pass can open and close without asking the driver. Deleting the
# bound framebuffer returns the binding to 0.
# Recorded frame (gl.SteinGlFrame; only active with the renderer in core): the game's glClear enters the list with the state of the moment
# (depth cleared before the hand) and marks that the jar has these rules; the clear color and depth are noted
# for that. Uploading, copying, reading or deleting a game texture is a sync point (the list goes to the driver first). With the
# renderer off, the same call as always.
# The game's objects on the API (gfx/game/SteinGameGl): the OpenGL calls the game still makes by itself
# (textures, framebuffers and renderbuffers, buffers, shaders, queries). With OpenGL each one goes to the
# driver as before (the hooks above still run); with Vulkan there is no context and they reach the
# emulation (SteinGameTextures, SteinGameFramebuffers) or answer what OpenGL would.
